chats.answer:
For a MacBook Pro + gaming PC sharing one 4K 144Hz monitor, I'd recommend a DisplayPort 1.4 KVM with DSC or an HDMI 2.1 KVM rated for 4K 144Hz or higher.

The important part is preserving your gaming PC's full refresh rate while allowing the MacBook to switch to the same monitor, keyboard, and mouse.

A few things to watch for:

4K 144Hz: Must explicitly support this resolution and refresh rate, not merely "4K 60Hz."

VRR / G-Sync / FreeSync: Important if you want variable refresh rate gaming.

MacBook compatibility: Most MacBook Pros output video over USB-C/Thunderbolt, so you may need a USB-C-to-DisplayPort 1.4 adapter or HDMI 2.1 connection.

USB peripherals: A KVM can switch your keyboard, mouse, and other USB devices together with the display.

chats.answer:
For a MacBook Pro + gaming PC sharing one 4K 144Hz monitor, I'd recommend a DisplayPort 1.4 KVM with DSC or an HDMI 2.1 KVM rated for 4K 144Hz or higher.

The key is maintaining your gaming PC's full refresh rate while switching your monitor, keyboard, and mouse between the two computers.

There are two good approaches:

DisplayPort 1.4 + DSC: Great for gaming PCs with DisplayPort outputs. Can support 4K 144Hz with compression.

HDMI 2.1: Often simpler when your MacBook Pro has an HDMI 2.1 port. Look for 48Gbps bandwidth and explicit 4K 144Hz support.

Avoid generic KVMs labeled only "4K supported." Many are limited to 4K 60Hz.
